plan.summary: This 4-week block is a simple off-camp build for a beginner boxer with one 45-minute S&C session per week and high skill practice priority. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the main lower-body strength pattern with a safe rep-max assessment, and the main training starts in Week 2. The block keeps the order power first, then strength, then upper-body and trunk accessories, with low equipment demands and fatigue kept under control so sparring stays the priority.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic force and power with simple bodyweight movements that are easy to recover from alongside boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress unilateral strength and explosive intent while keeping the weekly workload tight and recoverable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and shift more emphasis toward crisp speed and sharp explosive output.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Reset between reps. Jump as high and fast as you can and land quietly with control.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if space is tight. Start from a still quarter squat and jump hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Snap Down to Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if jump skill is limited. Stick the landing before the next rep.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled warm-up progression, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side using bodyweight tempo or range that makes the set challenging. Log the variation and reps so future work can be compared.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your hardest clean set of 3-5 reps per side. Use the toughest bodyweight version you can perform with good balance and depth, and log the variation and reps.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the hardest clean assessment set on each side with the exact variation used.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a bench or step is available and balance is solid.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats bother the knees. Keep the stride long and torso tall.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Leave 1-2 good reps in reserve. Keep ribs down, body straight, and press fast from the bottom.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if floor push-ups are not yet clean for the full rep range.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if regular push-ups are too easy.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
exercises.notes: Move slowly and keep the shoulders away from the ears. Clean positions matter more than height.

substitutionOptions.name: Floor Snow Angel
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the Y-T-W pattern is hard to organize. Stay smooth and controlled.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Lower back stays lightly pressed down. Shorten the lever if you cannot hold position cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if hollow holds cause lower-back discomfort.

substitutionOptions.name: Tuck Hollow Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full position is too hard.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Each rep should look sharp. Stop early if jump height or landing quality drops.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need a simpler option with less rhythm demand.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the bodyweight version that matched your assessment. Control the descent, hit full depth you can own, and stand up with intent.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the strongest clean set on each side using the same variation as Week 1.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need more difficulty and can stay balanced.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the fixed split stance feels awkward.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stop with 1-2 reps in reserve. Keep the body rigid and drive up fast.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot keep clean reps through all sets.

substitutionOptions.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if standard push-ups are too easy and shoulders feel good.

exercises.name: Towel Row Isometric
exercises.notes: Loop a towel around a sturdy post or use a partner-resistant pull. Brace hard and pull elbows back without shrugging.

substitutionOptions.name: Doorframe Row Isometric
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if the setup is solid and safe.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Back Extension Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you do not have a safe rowing setup.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Keep head, ribs, and hips in one line. Do not let the top shoulder roll forward.

substitutionOptions.name: Bent-Knee Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the full version is too hard.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
exercises.notes: Pause briefly in the quarter squat before takeoff. Explode up and land softly.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if squat jumps feel too stiff or awkward.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Own the bottom position and keep the front foot flat. If bodyweight is too easy, slow the lowering to 3 seconds.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the best quality set and note whether you used standard tempo or a slower lowering.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you need more challenge and can keep balance.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if split squats feel repetitive on the hips.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Smooth down, aggressive up. Stop before the hips sag or the head reaches first.

substitutionOptions.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if regular push-ups are now easy for all sets.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rep quality breaks early.

exercises.name: Prone Y-T-W Raise
exercises.notes: Small clean reps. Keep the neck relaxed and move from the upper back.

substitutionOptions.name: Floor Snow Angel
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if it is easier to perform well.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Rock
exercises.notes: Only use a range you can hold without losing lower-back position. Regress to a static hold if needed.

substitutionOptions.name: Hollow Body Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if rocking causes the position to break.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you feel strain in the lower back.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Keep every rep fast and clean. This week is about staying sharp, not adding fatigue.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you prefer a simpler jump pattern.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use the same variation as recent weeks but do fewer total reps. Keep the movement crisp and leave plenty in the tank.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track an easy strong set with clean form so the next block can build from it.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Lunge
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a fresh variation during the deload week.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Clean reps only. Finish each set feeling like you could do more.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if shoulders or wrists feel beat up.

exercises.name: Towel Row Isometric
exercises.notes: Brace and pull hard enough to feel the upper back, but keep the effort submaximal this week.

substitutionOptions.name: Prone Back Extension Hold
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you do not have a solid setup.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Stay stacked and steady. Treat this as trunk maintenance, not a test.

substitutionOptions.name: Bent-Knee Side Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want an easier recovery-week option.
